findings: VERIFIED GREEN: I copied the repo to /tmp, ran `uv sync --frozen` and the gates. `uv run pytest -q` gives 249 passed, 1 skipped (baseline was 182/1), `run_mock_test.py` passes, `python -m evals.offline_eval` prints the five-metric table and writes report.json, and `--check-baseline` reproduces evals/baseline.json exactly (+0.000 on all five). No protected path touched (no pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .github), no new dependency, no secret in fixtures. Tests are pure additions: 718 lines added, zero test lines deleted or loosened. M1 (G1) is genuinely done, not just claimed.

CORPUS IS SYNTHETIC, NOT THE RECORDED RUNS: G1 says the harness replays 'the recorded search results in evals/runs/**'. evals/runs/ does not exist in the repo (gitignored), so T-0001 hand-wrote 23 records under evals/fixtures/ using .example domains and invented page text. README states the reasoning, and the charter does sanction evals/fixtures/** for captured lessons, so this is a defensible reading — but metric absolutes describe made-up pages. Only deltas on this corpus mean anything, and nothing in the corpus came from a live Brave response.

THE G2 GATE IS NOW UNREACHABLE AS WRITTEN: T-0004 froze aggregator_drop_rate, location_match_rate and staleness_detection_rate at 1.000. M2 and G2's definition of done require improvement on posting-shape rate AND aggregator-drop rate with no metric regressing; aggregator-drop is already at the ceiling and cannot improve. It is maxed partly by definition: the denominator counts only records labelled aggregator AND kind=index, of which the whole corpus has two (the backend profile scores n/a). Aggregator pages labelled kind=posting — e.g. the kept de.indeed.com/viewjob record — are excluded from the metric entirely. Unless a future task adds harder aggregator cases to the corpus, G2 can never be reported as done, and the agents chose both the corpus and the baseline themselves.

T-0006 [G2] MOVED NO MEASURED METRIC: it added ~70 lines of per-vendor URL parsing in src/url_heuristics.py for 12 hosts that have zero records in the corpus. Its own commit message concedes the corpus 'cannot itself show a metric delta', and --check-baseline confirms all five metrics unchanged. The work plausibly serves G2's intent (board index pages consuming result budget), but it is the largest body of new deciding logic added in 24 hours with no offline measurement behind it — G2's done condition explicitly requires every change to be covered by an offline test that fails without it, and while the URL unit tests do fail on revert, the harness that is supposed to be 'the measure' is blind to all of it.

LIVE LESSON NOT CAPTURED AS A FIXTURE: T-0006's commit message says the URL shapes were verified against live Brave Search results. The charter constraint is that when a live call teaches you something, capture it as a fixture under evals/fixtures/** so the harness keeps the lesson. The shapes were saved only as URL string literals inside tests/test_url_heuristics.py, not as corpus records, so the next agent still cannot measure these hosts and the money spent on those live searches bought no harness coverage.

UNMEASURED FALSE-POSITIVE RISK FROM T-0006: the new hosts are matched as bare substrings of the hostname. I confirmed against the merged code that classify_url('https://acme-talent.com/careers') returns index and is_aggregator_url returns True, same for 'https://careers.globaltalent.com/jobs/engineer', and 'https://www.mytalent.com/view?id=1' is forced to posting by the talent.com branch. With the default exclude_aggregator_sites=true, a company career site whose domain merely ends in 'talent.com' is now dropped outright. 'neuvoo.', 'simplyhired.', 'careerjet.' and 'jobsora.' carry the same collision shape. The substring style is pre-existing, but the new entries are far more collision-prone, this runs against G2 (losing genuine direct postings), and no corpus record or test covers it.

REPLAY IS FAITHFUL BUT FLATTENS PRIORITY: replay_keep calls the real url_heuristics/page_signals functions and matches the default production config, so it is not a copy of the rules. One divergence worth knowing: Orchestrator._triage_urls down-ranks aggregator postings and non-aggregator board index pages rather than dropping them, and only crawls them if budget remains; the harness counts them as flatly 'kept'. So posting_shape_rate is slightly pessimistic versus what a budget-limited production run would actually surface. Not a defect, but the number is not quite the thing its name suggests.

PROCESS AND COST: 46 agent runs, 31 sandbox denials and $31.46 for 6 merges. I cannot see what the denials were, so I cannot judge whether any were attempts to work around a restriction. No sign of repeated failure on the same task — the six merges are sequential and distinct. T-0007 sits parked carrying a reviewer note that begins 'approve: Independently verified' and confirms scope, paths, no deps and no secrets, so an approved G2 change is idle in the queue; the note itself is truncated mid-sentence, which may be why it never merged. Nothing was merged outside G1/G2, and G3 has not been started, which matches the charter's priority order.

ASSUMPTION RECORDED: I judged 'no metric regressing' by re-running the committed baseline gate, not by recomputing the arming-time numbers independently, since no harness existed at arming to produce them. The arming baseline is therefore whatever T-0004 measured after T-0001–T-0003 defined the corpus.
digest: Six merges, all inside G1 and G2. I ran the gates myself: tests are green at 249 passed / 1 skipped (up from 182), the mock loop passes, the offline harness runs with no network and reproduces its committed baseline exactly. No protected files, no new dependencies, no test was deleted or weakened. M1 is really done. Two things need your eye. First, the corpus is 23 hand-written synthetic pages, not the recorded runs the charter names, and the frozen baseline already pins aggregator-drop at 1.000 — so G2's stated finish line, an improvement on that metric, is now impossible without new corpus cases. Second, T-0006 shipped 70 lines of vendor URL rules for 12 hosts the corpus never touches; by its own commit message it moves no metric, the live Brave findings behind it were never saved as fixtures, and its hostname matching is loose enough that a real company site like acme-talent.com is now dropped as an aggregator. An approved task, T-0007, is sitting parked. Nothing has left the charter; the measurement is just drifting ahead of what it can prove.
